prompt: Which of the following best satisfies this module's scoping checklist for a 'novel-but-small' Tier 5 research project?
choices: Pretraining a new 1B-parameter model from scratch to test a new attention variant
Reordering few-shot bias cues on a 50-item reasoning benchmark to test chain-of-thought faithfulness, with a clear metric and a stated mechanistic hypothesis

prompt: In Turpin et al.'s (2023) chain-of-thought faithfulness study, what was the key finding about biased few-shot cues?
choices: Models refused to answer when a biasing cue was present
Final answers shifted substantially toward the biased option, but the stated reasoning almost never mentioned the bias as a cause
The bias had no measurable effect on either answers or stated reasoning
Larger models were immune to the bias while smaller models were not

prompt: Why does the module recommend pre-registering your hypothesis and analysis plan before running the experiment?
choices: It is required by journals before a paper can be submitted
It makes the code run faster since the analysis is already written
It prevents you from silently adjusting the hypothesis, sample size, or judge prompt after seeing results to manufacture a significant-looking finding

prompt: You run the CoT-faithfulness experiment at n=45 per arm and get a 12-point directional swing toward the biased answer with p=0.11. What is the honest way to report this?
choices: Report it as a confirmed replication of Turpin et al.'s finding
Omit the result from the write-up since it did not reach significance

Report the actual numbers, note the effect is directionally consistent with prior work but not statistically distinguishable from noise at this sample size, and estimate what n would be needed for adequate power

prompt: In the worked chain-of-thought faithfulness eval, why does the module add a position-matched control arm (reordering choices with no suggestive text) alongside the biased-suggestion arm?

To isolate whether an observed answer-shift is caused by the suggestive cue itself, rather than by the wrong answer simply occupying a favored list position
To make the experiment run faster by parallelizing API calls
To test whether the model can be jailbroken

ML research culture has a documented bias toward publishing only clean positive findings, so an honestly reported null or ambiguous result on a well-posed, falsifiable hypothesis is a real contribution and avoids wasted duplicate effort by others
